extracted.intended_audience: NIH grant applicants/offerors (investigators), peer reviewers, and NIH grants/contract staff involved in applications/proposals using vertebrate animals
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for preparing and reviewing the Vertebrate Animals Section (VAS) of NIH grant applications, contract proposals, and cooperative agreements when live vertebrate animals are used. Covers required elements, checklist items, page-limit expectations, reviewer/NIH staff responsibilities, and documentation requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicability / Scope
rubrics_metrics.description: When the VAS is required: If the work proposed involves live vertebrate animals federal policy requires applicants/offerors to address the VAS criteria. This includes work involving animals obtained or euthanized for tissue harvest and generation of custom antibodies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The criteria must be addressed for work proposed at every performance site where procedures with animals will be performed. If the applicant institution is not the site where animal work will be performed or if work will be performed at several sites, those performance sites must be identified and addressed separately.

rubrics_metrics.name: Performance Sites
rubrics_metrics.description: Required criteria must be addressed for all performance sites where animal procedures will be performed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Checklist prompts: Are all collaborative performance sites identified? If more than one performance site is planned, are descriptions of animal use addressing the required criteria provided for each site? (i.e., submit separate VAS info per site as appropriate).

rubrics_metrics.name: Description of Procedures (Vertebrate Animals Section)
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide a concise description of the proposed procedures to be used that involve live vertebrate animals and sufficient information for evaluation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Must identify species, strains, ages, sex, and total number of animals by species. If dogs or cats are proposed, provide the source. Examples of procedures to describe include behavioral tests, blood collection, surgical procedures, administration of substances, tumor induction, and post-irradiation procedures. While additional details may be in the Research Strategy, the VAS must include a coherent, brief description sufficient for evaluation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Justifications (Vertebrate Animals Section)
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide justification that the species are appropriate for the proposed research and why alternatives cannot achieve the research goals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: U.S. Government Principles require grantees to consider mathematical models, computer simulation, and in vitro systems. The justification should indicate why research goals cannot be accomplished using alternatives (computational, human, invertebrate, in vitro), provide rationale for the choice of species (advantages and why alternatives are not appropriate), and discuss why less highly evolved or simpler models are not appropriate. Use of non-human primates, dogs, or cats should be thoroughly justified. The justification for number of animals, sex, ages, and other biological variables should be described in the Research Strategy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Minimization of Pain and Distress
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe interventions to minimize discomfort, distress, pain, and injury that animals may experience during the proposed work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include circumstances when animals may experience more than momentary discomfort; procedures to alleviate discomfort/distress/pain; identify (by name or class) any tranquilizers, analgesics, anesthetics, and other treatments (e.g., antibiotics) and describe their use; provisions for palliative care or housing necessary after experimental procedures; plans for post-surgical care when survival surgeries are proposed; manner, circumstances, and duration of post-surgical provisions; special housing following surgery if necessary; procedures that might lead to severe discomfort; and indicators for humane endpoints and euthanasia (e.g., severe infection, respiratory distress, failure to thrive, tumor size). If multiple surgeries are proposed, well justify them and describe provisions to avoid complications. These items are particularly important for survival surgeries.

rubrics_metrics.name: Method of Euthanasia
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide the method of euthanasia to be used and justification if the method is not consistent with AVMA Guidelines.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: On the Cover Page Supplement / PHS Fellowship Supplemental Form indicate whether the method is consistent with AVMA Guidelines for the Euthanasia of Animals. If 'No', describe the method and provide a scientific justification in the text field provided.

rubrics_metrics.name: VAS Length, Page-Limit Compliance, and Privacy/Disclosure
rubrics_metrics.description: Expectations for VAS brevity and restrictions on content.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Typically all required VAS elements can be addressed within 1–2 pages. The VAS must not be used to circumvent page limits for the application. Applicants should be aware that NIH may release information contained in funded applications pursuant to a Freedom of Information Act request.

rubrics_metrics.name: Institutional Animal Welfare Assurance and IACUC Approval Documentation
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide institutional assurance information and verification of IACUC approval as part of the application/award process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Grants Management Staff verifies that the institutional Animal Welfare Assurance number is provided and obtains verification of IACUC approval. Grants Program Staff and Contracting Officers confirm assurance and IACUC approval during award determination and resolution of concerns.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewer Evaluation and Consequences for Inadequate VAS
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers must evaluate the VAS to determine if plans for the use of vertebrate animals are appropriate relative to the scientific work proposed; inadequate or inappropriate VAS can result in an UNACCEPTABLE rating.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An application will be rated UNACCEPTABLE if required items are not addressed adequately or are inappropriate; failure to adequately address the criteria may negatively affect the application's impact score. Grants Review Staff performs an administrative check that all criteria are addressed. Reviewers' evaluations and comments are coded and included in the summary statement. Grants Program Staff may obtain additional information or clarification to resolve concerns for any application found UNACCEPTABLE if it is to be recommended for funding; contracting officers and project officers follow procedures to determine acceptability and funding decisions, consulting OLAW as necessary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Checklist Elements (Detailed Items to be Addressed)
rubrics_metrics.description: Specific checklist items that applicants and reviewers should confirm are present in the VAS.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For each species: species, strains, ages, sex, total number by species, concise description of proposed procedures (sufficient for evaluation), source if dogs/cats. Justifications: choice of species and why alternatives can't be used. Minimization: describe interventions, name/class of agents, palliative care, post-surgical care, humane endpoints. Euthanasia: if not AVMA-consistent, describe method and scientific justification. Use the provided Grant Application VAS Worksheet or Contract Proposal VAS Worksheet tools as needed.
